mechaber/1:main: Not to drink after the 4 cups. Containing 2 paragraphs: After the four cups, he is not allowed to drink wine, but rather water. {Rama: And the law of all drinks (besides water) is like [the law concerning] wine (Beit Yosef). And one who is delicate or greatly desires to drink may drink a fifth cup [of wine] and say the Great Hallel upon it (Mordekhai}.}
mechaber/2:main: A person is obligated to engage in the laws of Passover and the story of the Exodus from Egypt, and to recount the miracles and wonders that the Holy One, Blessed be He, performed for our ancestors until sleep overtakes him. {Rama: And all the laws of the first night also apply to the second night (Agur}. It is customary to recite only the Shema before going to sleep and not the other passages that are usually recited on other nights, in order to provide protection, as this is a ‘night of watching’ from harmful forces.}
baer-heitev/1:א: (א) Thus. Darkei Moshe wrote that the custom is to permit drinking kreiznach in our country, and even apfel trank is permitted, end of his words. And Magen Avraham wrote that this means that apfel trank that they make in our country by cooking water with apples; but that trank that they make in the land of Ashkenaz where they crush the apples in the press and it has a strong taste, there is to forbid. And ginger water that they call ingber vasser, there is to permit, per Magen Avraham and Kaf HaChayim who brought that it is permitted to drink all beverages that are not intoxicating, and so too in Beiur Halacha and the author of Peri Chadash, see there. Therefore it is clear to permit drinking coffee or tea and the like. And Knesset HaGedolah in his book Pesach Me'uvin wrote that he did not want to practice permitting drinking coffee and drinking tobacco that they call tabak — he wrote that one who guards his soul shall distance himself from it.
baer-heitev/1:ב: (ב) The Great. And if he didn't say the big praise for the D. M:
baer-heitev/2:א: (א) 2. And for the other two, you can drink all the rest of the three cups
baer-heitev/2:ב: (ב) Shma. And one must recite the blessing of hamapil, per Mahariv. And if he read kerias shma in the synagogue before night, he must read the entire kerias shma in order to fulfill siman 235.
beer-hagolah/1:_: A column called his father, Joseph, was good at them, and that all the geniuses were written
beer-hagolah/2:_: A column called for an addition from the Old Testament of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, etc
machatzit-hashekel/1:_: In Magen Avraham, may his memory be blessed, Darkei Moshe etc.; and it is possible that he holds etc.; and Peri Chadash disagrees and wrote that in any case the reason is not that he nullifies the taste of matzah, for behold he already drank the last two cups, and in any case the taste of matzah was nullified. Rather the reason is so that he should not become intoxicated and sleep, and it is a mitzvah to increase in recounting the praises of the Holy One Blessed be He; and according to this, all beverages that are not intoxicating are permitted to drink, and how much more so coffee, as is the current custom.
machatzit-hashekel/2:_: (Seif katan 2) Only etc. In the Gemara, chapter HaRo'eh, daf 60b — birkas hamapil and more, it is not fitting to say that it is for guarding, and it appears that he does not believe, Heaven forbid, in the words of our Sages, may their memory be blessed, that it is a night of guarding.
magen-avraham/1:_: Thus Darkei Moshe. And Mahariv wrote that water that was cooked, which they call apfel trank, is inferior to wine and forbidden because it nullifies the taste of matzah; and the custom is to drink water cooked with sweet roots that they call kreiznach — and if so, it is possible that apfel trank is also permitted, end of Darkei Moshe's words. And it appears to me that Mahariv forbade only those that they make in the land of Ashkenaz where they crush apples in the press and they have a strong taste; but in our country where they cook water with apples, our law is like kreiznach. And Bach wrote that it is possible that kreiznach is also forbidden; but in ginger water that they call ingber vasser I have not seen to forbid, end of his words. And it is possible that he holds that perhaps anything on which water was placed is permitted. Great Hallel. It appears to me specifically when he did not say the Great Hallel on the fourth cup.
magen-avraham/2:_: Only parshas Shma. It appears to me that if he read kerias shma in the synagogue by day, he must read at night the entire kerias shma in order to fulfill eighteen, as is written siman 235; and if he read it in the synagogue at night, he need not read except parshas Shma, since it is mentioned explicitly in the Gemara, chapter HaRo'eh. And Mahariv wrote that one must say birkas hamapil. And Maharil wrote that one should not lock the door with a strong bolt, and where damage is common we do not rely on a forced circumstance.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (א) He is not permitted, etc. — there are many reasons for this among the poskim: some wrote because of the mitzvah to recount the Exodus and the wonders of the Holy One Blessed be He even all night until sleep seizes him, as below — therefore he should not drink lest he become intoxicated and be nullified from this mitzvah; according to this reasoning, only wine or another intoxicating beverage; some wrote lest it appear that he adds to the cups, as though beginning another meal — according to this, all strong wine of the country is forbidden even if it is not intoxicating; some wrote lest the taste of matzah be nullified from his mouth through his drinking, as they forbade eating after the seder for this reason — according to this reason, any beverage, even if it is not strong wine of the country and is not intoxicating, is forbidden; from the conclusion of the words of the Mechaber and Rama it appears that their opinion is to be stringent for all these reasons; nevertheless the Acharonim wrote that ingber vasser and the like, and similarly tea or apfel trank, and some wrote that kreiznach is also permitted, for this does not nullify the taste of matzah and is like ordinary water [however for apfel trank that crushes the apples in the press and has a strong taste, some forbid]. And behold, even though l'chatchila it is proper to be stringent regarding anything that nullifies the taste of matzah, nevertheless in a situation of great need one may rely on the first reasoning to permit him to drink other beverages that are not intoxicating; and especially on the second night, certainly one may be lenient regarding other beverages that are not intoxicating.
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (ב) One who greatly desires to drink — even wine.
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (ג) And he says upon it the Great Hallel — specifically if he has not yet finished the berachah and drank the fourth cup, then he may say the Great Hallel until the end and conclude with berachah and drink the fifth cup; but if he already finished the conclusion of the berachah, he may not return to say the Great Hallel and bless at the end, for they enacted only one berachah.
mishnah-berurah/2:_: (ד) Shema — and he must bless Birkas Hamapil; and if he read Shema in synagogue before the night, he must read all of Shema to fulfill, as siman 235.
turei-zahav/1:_: In the Tur he brings the words of Rabbeinu Hai regarding the fifth cup, as follows: one who wishes to drink the fifth cup shall say upon it the Great Hallel and leave yehalelucha and say it afterward (meaning: on the fourth cup he says Hallel and leaves yehalelucha on the fifth cup upon which he says the Great Hallel, and there he finishes yehalelucha); but now the disciples have come and said that on every cup one needs a blessing afterward as before it, and one says yehalelucha after Hallel and they conclude "the King Who is extolled with praises," and they drink the fifth cup and say upon it the Great Hallel and conclude in it "the soul of every living being" until "Who chooses." Beit Yosef expanded in explaining this matter, and it appears to me that the meaning is: certainly there is no concluding blessing on Hallel; rather initially the concluding blessing of "Who chooses" was also applicable to the Hallel that he said on the fourth cup, just as the final blessing that is on the vine is also applicable to the third cup — so too here with the concluding blessing; but since the disciples said that on the vine one needs on every cup, therefore also the concluding blessing of "Who chooses" is applicable only to the Great Hallel of the fifth cup, not to the Hallel of the fourth cup — you have no concluding blessing on Hallel; therefore perforce they concluded on the fourth cup with "the King Who is extolled" and on the fifth cup with "Who chooses," and he responded to this that it is not proper, for the Sages did not say two blessings — meaning two concluding blessings — but one of them; if so, why do we practice only on four cups and we conclude in yehalelucha "the King Who is extolled"? If one erred and concluded after yishtabach with "Who chooses," he should not again conclude after Nishmas with "the King Who is extolled," for behold even on two cups there would be only one concluding blessing — how much more so on one cup; rather he shall say the Great Hallel until the concluding blessing and no more — thus it appears to me, plainly. (1) And all beverages etc. Mahariv wrote that specifically water as it is, and not water that was cooked, such as apfel trank, for it nullifies the taste of matzah and is inferior to wine, therefore; and Mateh Moshe, may his memory be blessed, wrote, and it is possible that water of kreiznach is also forbidden. Ginger water that they call ingber vasser — it is to permit.
